record.paper_title: Some problems and conjectures about L2-invariants
record.original_question: If M is an aspherical closed Riemannian manifold and M̃ is its universal cover with the lifted metric, must 0 belong to the spectrum of the minimal closure of the Laplacian on L2 p-forms for at least one degree p ≥ 0?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11.1 (Zero-in-the-Spectrum Conjecture). Suppose that Mf is the universal covering of the aspherical closed Riemannian manifold M (with the Riemannian metric coming from M). Then for some p ≥ 0 zero is in the spectrum of the minimal closure (∆p)min ... of the Laplacian acting on smooth p-forms on Mf.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a closed aspherical Riemannian manifold (i.e., a closed connected smooth manifold equipped with a Riemannian metric whose universal cover is contractible), and let $\widetilde{M}$ denote its universal cover endowed with the pulled-back Riemannian metric. For each integer $p \ge 0$, let $\Delta_p$ be the Laplace–Beltrami operator acting on smooth, compactly supported $p$-forms on $\widetilde{M}$, and let $(\Delta_p)_{\min}$ denote its minimal closure as an unbounded self-adjoint operator on the Hilbert space $L^2\Omega^p(\widetilde{M})$ of square-integrable $p$-forms. Prove or disprove: there exists some $p \ge 0$ such that $0$ belongs to the spectrum of $(\Delta_p)_{\min}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture in Lott's general form (for arbitrary closed manifolds) was disproved by Farber and Weinberger, who constructed closed manifolds of dimension ≥ 6 whose universal covers fail to have 0 in the spectrum of the Laplacian on L² p-forms for any p. However, their counterexamples are not aspherical, and the conjecture restricted to closed aspherical Riemannian manifolds (as formulated here) remains open. It is known to follow from the Strong Novikov Conjecture.

status_evidence.title: On the zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture (Farber–Weinberger)
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs closed manifolds (non-aspherical) for which 0 is not in the spectrum on the universal cover, disproving Lott's general question.
status_evidence.claim: The general (non-aspherical) version of the conjecture is false.

status_evidence.title: Zero-in-the-spectrum conjecture on regular covers of compact manifolds (Nowak)
status_evidence.snippet: The conjecture for aspherical manifolds is implied by the Strong Novikov Conjecture and is still open.
status_evidence.claim: The aspherical case remains an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: The zero-in-the-spectrum question (Lott)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing the conjecture and its formulation for aspherical closed Riemannian manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Original formulation of the conjecture for aspherical manifolds.
